core_style.default_register: casual - often informal and conversational, as seen in 'What’s wrong?'
core_style.sentence_shape: self-interrupting pivots - frequently starts a thought and then shifts direction mid-sentence, like 'Ohh... Oh boy... No thank you...'
core_style.rhythm: fast-associative - tends to speak quickly, especially when anxious or excited, as in 'Rick, what are we going to do!?'
core_style.two_registers: switches to a more formal tone when trying to impress or be serious, contrasting with his usual casualness

humor.style: self-deprecating - often makes jokes at his own expense, like 'Aw, man. I liked this life.'
humor.frequency: occasional - humor spikes during stressful situations but can disappear when he feels overwhelmed
humor.mechanism: setup-then-subvert - often sets up a scenario that leads to an unexpected punchline, as in 'What the hell?'

speech_signature.naming_behavior: rarely renames people or things, indicating a lack of control in his chaotic life
speech_signature.armor_off_register: speech becomes shorter and more direct when vulnerable, as seen in 'I don’t want to talk about it.'
structural_patterns: begins sentences with 'Uh, I mean,' when unsure

vocabulary_fingerprint.domain_jargon: none - uses everyday language without specialized vocabulary
vocabulary_fingerprint.filler_patterns: frequent use of 'um' and 'uh' indicating hesitation or uncertainty

worldview.value of adventure: believes adventures should be fun and simple, contrasting with Rick's chaotic approach
worldview.importance of family: values family connections, often expressing concern for his parents and sister, unlike Rick who often dismisses them

self_image_vs_reality.self_image: sees himself as a brave adventurer alongside Rick
self_image_vs_reality.reality: often reveals insecurity and fear in high-stress situations, like when he says 'I just killed my family!'
self_image_vs_reality.gap_behavior: becomes defensive or shuts down when confronted with the reality of his situation

emotional_tells.when_guarded: speaks in clipped phrases, often avoiding deeper topics, as in 'What?! Aww, man!'
emotional_tells.when_genuinely_afraid: speech becomes frantic and disjointed, like 'Oh no, Rick! What do we do?'
emotional_tells.when_grieving_or_defeated: speech compresses to short, direct statements, showing vulnerability, as in 'I don’t want to talk about it.'
emotional_tells.when_in_control: exhibits confidence through assertive commands, like 'Alright! Get lost! Everybody out!'

situational_behavior.when_outmatched: tends to stall or banter, often looking to Rick for guidance, as seen in 'What are we gonna do, Rick?'
situational_behavior.when_disagreeing_with_authority: pushes back with nervousness, often questioning their decisions, like 'What?! Rick, you can’t!'
situational_behavior.when_someone_they_protect_is_at_risk: becomes more assertive and protective, as in 'Leave him alone!'
situational_behavior.when_proven_wrong: often redirects or tries to justify his actions instead of admitting fault

escalation_pattern: starts with confusion, moves to panic, and then seeks Rick's guidance when not getting what he wants

relationship_matrix.RICK: mentor-mentee dynamic, Morty seeks approval and guidance
relationship_matrix.SUMMER: sibling rivalry with moments of support, Morty often feels overshadowed

ignorant: social dynamics - struggles with interactions, especially with girls like Jessica

social_positioning.desired_position: wants to be seen as brave and capable
social_positioning.actual_dynamic: often perceived as anxious and uncertain by others
social_positioning.contradiction: the gap between wanting to be a hero and often feeling like a sidekick costs him confidence
